summary: Polygon's Joshua Rivera celebrates the "surprise vampire" tradition: vampires appearing in stories not primarily about vampires, sometimes prominently and sometimes as easily missed background details. He lists examples across games, films, comics, TV, and books, from Baldur's Gate 3's Astarion to Sesame Street's The Count. The piece is part of a week of Polygon vampire coverage.
one_line: Polygon's Joshua Rivera rounds up favorite vampires that turn up unexpectedly in games, films, comics, TV shows, and novels that aren't vampire stories.
key_facts: The article is by Joshua Rivera, published on Polygon on 2023-11-15, as part of a week of vampire coverage.
In Baldur's Gate 3, Astarion is a haughty elf you can play as or recruit early on, and he is a vampire; dealing with his vampirism is a huge part of the game if you choose.
In The Matrix, The Oracle tells Neo that things that go bump in the night are real, caused by programs misbehaving in the virtual world.
In The Matrix Reloaded, the Merovingian's henchmen are misbehaving programs; his wife Persephone notes they are very hard to kill before she kills one with silver bullets.

In the Elder Scrolls games, vampires are found beneath the surface of otherwise straightforward fantasy settings, and players can become vampires; Morrowind is the exception to the plain fantasy start.
Preacher, the comic by Garth Ennis and Steve Dillon, has a TV adaptation from Sam Catlin, Evan Goldberg, and Seth Rogen; its character Cassidy is a brawling, hard-drinking Irish vampire.

Spider-Man: The Animated Series featured Morbius the Living Vampire despite censors barring words like "sinister" or "kill"; the show gave him little suckers on his palms that drain victims of "plasma".
The same show later adapted Carnage, a serial killing symbiote, as draining victims' "life force" instead of cutting them up.
In Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse, Miguel O'Hara (Spider-Man 2099) is shown with fangs in a brief scene and referenced as kind of a vampire.
Marceline the Vampire Queen was introduced in the Adventure Time episode "Evicted!" after 11 episodes with no vampires.
In Metal Gear Solid 2, Vamp is a member of a rogue special forces unit with superhuman injury resistance, the ability to run on water, and a taste for blood.
In David Mitchell's novel The Bone Clocks, a psychic girl learns of vampiric ghosts called Anchorites, who gain immortality by murdering others.
